Class MenuSwitch

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.menu.MenuSwitch
public final class MenuSwitch extends Object
Switching a player between menus while one menu, the one they opened in the world, waits open behind the others. For tabs on a container screen: a player at a chest flips to their inventory, a shulker box, their ender chest, and back, and the chest stays open in the world the whole time (its lid up, no close sound), while every other menu really closes when they leave it (the inventory's crafting grid hands its items back). 
// Server, from a tab click:
MenuSwitch.open(player, boxProvider);     // the chest waits behind, the box opens
MenuSwitch.openInventory(player);         // the box closes, the inventory opens
MenuSwitch.back(player);                  // the inventory closes, the chest comes back

// Common init: hear when the waiting menu closes on its own.
MenuSwitch.onSetAsideClosed((player, menu, why) -> ...);

The menu set aside

The first switch away from a menu the player opened some other way (a chest they clicked, any player.openMenu that isn't this class's) sets it aside instead of closing it: no removed(), no close packet, so the block's opener count holds. Menus opened through open(ServerPlayer, MenuProvider) are the tabs: switching away from one closes it normally. The inventory is never set aside, so a switch that starts at the inventory screen sets nothing aside, and back(ServerPlayer) has nothing to return to. Only a menu opened through openMenu can be set aside (its title is what back shows again); any other closes normally.

While it waits, the set-aside menu's stillValid is checked every tick, and it closes properly (removed(), so the lid shuts) when that fails, the player dies or changes dimension, the menu in front closes (Escape on any screen), a menu opens some other way, or the player leaves. onSetAsideClosed(MenuSwitch.SetAsideClosed) hears each of these. It gets no sync while it waits; back resyncs it whole.

The cursor

The stack on the cursor moves across every switch, to the next menu, instead of going back to the inventory.

The client

open and back send only vanilla packets, so they work for a player without SlotKit. openInventory(ServerPlayer) needs SlotKit on the client (vanilla has no packet that opens the inventory) and returns false without it. With SlotKit on the client, the screen the player is on stays up until the next menu's contents arrive, so a switch never shows an empty screen for a frame.

Server thread only. Since 2.1.0.

    • open

      public static OptionalInt open(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, net.minecraft.world.MenuProvider next)
      Opens next for player. The menu in front is set aside if it can be (see the class doc) and nothing is set aside yet, and otherwise closes normally. The cursor stack moves to next.
      Returns:
      the new menu's container id, or empty when next made no menu. Then the player goes back to the set-aside menu, or with none, the screen closes and the cursor stack returns to the inventory.
